The original test code (which I saw earlier when reading the file) was trying to manually parse each child's name to extract the left and right parent identifiers and the t‑parameter, building a `keys` set to detect duplicates. It looked something like:

```
children = build_generation(parents, 1, evaluate)
keys = set()
for child in children:
    left, right, t_part = child.name.removeprefix("gen1_").rpartition("@t")[0], None, None
    assert child.name not in keys
    keys.add(child.name)
names = [child.name for child in children]
```

That approach is unnecessarily complex for simply checking that there are no duplicate names. I can achieve the same verification more cleanly by just collecting all child names into a list and asserting that the length of that list equals the length of the set of names—if any duplicates exist, the set will be smaller.

```

names = [child.name for child in children]
```
